interactions.summary: Jiang says fraud makes promises, contracts, and cooperation impossible, then the reading moves into the simoniacs and Dante's anger at church corruption.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang plus student reading Dante aloud

claims.claim: Jiang says a fraudulent world makes it impossible to make promises, contracts, or cooperative social arrangements.
The canto 19 reading introduces simony as the sale of sacred things for gold and silver, focusing Dante's anger on ecclesiastical corruption.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted poem read in class on 2026-06-23.

signature_moments.moment: Fraud is said to destroy the very possibility of promising and contracting with one another.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This states the social cost of fraud in the strongest possible terms and links Dante's moral category to institutional breakdown.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The sale of sacred goods or offices for money, here introduced as a paradigmatic church corruption.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture moves from generic fraud to an institutionalized form of fraud inside sacred authority: simony.
